observations: body L1-L10: the rules render al-Battānī's text of chapter 25 (p. 37) for a star and a degree on opposite sides of the equator, step by step, with the quantity he calls divisum; L9 is L6 put into L7.
body L3-L4: the minus signs are printed as long dashes (9.7 and 10.0 pt); they are set as minus signs.
body L5: a short raised bar, a speck, stands between ε and the second sin of the numerator.
body L7: a mark like an acute accent, a speck, stands over the e of «aeq.».
body L14: the dash of «22–31» is a long dash (5.1 pt).
body L16: in the letter-spaced «Regiomontanus» the o after gi is printed broken, open at the top, and a blot stands under the g.

body L16-L22: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIII) correct this passage and note 1: the letter is not Regiomontanus' to Bianchini, as Delambre affirms, but Bianchini's to Regiomontanus, now better edited by M. Curtze, Urkunden zur Geschichte der Mathematik im Mittelalter und der Renaissance, Leipzig 1902, t. I, p. 240–41. They quote its passage on a rule for the declination of a star that has latitude, which Bianchini doubts and finds stated by Albategni without a proof. The printed text is kept.

body L20: the minus signs of Delambre's fraction are printed as long dashes (10.4 and 10.1 pt); they are set as minus signs. When the culminating degree is a solstice, as on the colure of the solstices, δ′ = ε, the sinus crescens equals the sinus longissimus and their ratio in the rules is 1.
body L23: the heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which continues on the next page.
body L24-L26: the first objection holds: the rules of the two cases (p. 197 and L1-L10) differ in form, not only by δ + δ′ in place of δ − δ′.

body L26-L28: the minus signs of L26 are printed as long dashes (9.7 and 10.1 pt); they are set as minus signs. The dash of «al–Battānī» is a long dash (5.5 pt), the dash before «2°.» measures 10.2 pt.

body L28-L33: the second objection holds: by L5 the sine of the obliquitas aequata has cos (δ + δ′) in its denominator, which vanishes when δ + δ′ = 90°; this can happen, since δ′ is at most ε and a star on the other side of the equator may have δ = 90° − δ′. The value exceeds R before that (with ε = δ′ = 23° 30′ and δ = 60° it is 2.8 R), and no arc has such a sine.
notes_left L1: corrected with L16-L22 in the addenda (p. LXXIII): the letter that Nallino could not read is Bianchini's to Regiomontanus, edited by Curtze.
notes_right L4: the hyphen of «obscu-» is printed short (1.7 pt), like a point.
notes_right L5: a broken mark like a bar stands before «vel»; the hyphen of «Regio-» is printed low and short (2.3 pt), like a point.
